[ASSISTANT_SAID] Congratulations on completing your interview at the US Citizenship and Immigration Services office!  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tailoring your resume to the US job market requires adjustments to make it appealing to American employers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for tailoring a resume include:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Use a reverse chronological format.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Keep it concise and to the point (1-2 pages).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Use keywords and phrases from the job posting.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Quantify achievements (e.g., "Increased sales by 25% in 6 months").  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Emphasize transferable skills.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. Include relevant sections (summary, education, work experience, skills, certifications).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 7. Use action verbs (e.g., "Managed," "Created," "Developed").  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 8. Proofread and edit multiple times.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 9. Tailor your resume to each job.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 10. Get familiar with US job market norms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips include using a standard font (Arial, Calibri, Helvetica), bullet points, including a LinkedIn profile, and being prepared to explain gaps in employment or education.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] By following these tips, you'll be well on your way to creating a US-style resume.  
[USER] User found the resume tips helpful and wants to know more about preparing for a job interview in the US.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Preparing for a job interview in the US is crucial for making a good impression.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for preparing for a job interview include:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Research the company and its culture.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Review the job description.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Prepare specific examples using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Practice responses to common interview questions.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Dress professionally.
